To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SAMTEX data have been used to construct images of electrical resistivities and anisotropies at 100 and 200 km.

the electrical conductivity of the lithospheric roots of cratons is primarily controlled by the temperature, iron content and composition of their bulk matrix, and that the electrical resistivity is spatially correlated with seismic velocity.

(i) the subcontinental lithospheric mantles of the southern African cratons are characterized by high resistivities and isotropic resistivity anisotropic tensors; (ii) the subcontinental mantle beneath the mobile belts are characterized by lower resistivities and anisotropic resistivity anisotrpy tensors; (iii) the resistivity anisometry of the subcontinental mantle is a function of the degree to which it is deformed, and the direction and degree of deformation are controlled
In summary, our research is concerned with

the use of magnetotelluricity to identify areas where kimberlite magmatism is likely to occur, and with the use of seismic velocities and electrical resistivities to constrain physical parameters of the sub- continental lithospheric mantle.
the development of new techniques for the analysis of large MT datasets.

understanding the electrical resistivity variations within southern Africa, particularly the southern part of the Kaapvaa Craton, and how these variations are controlled by the physical properties and conditions of the lithospheric materials, and how these properties and conditions control kimberlite emplacement and diamond formation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
diamonds form in the sub-continental mantle, and that they are more likely to occur where the lithosphere has a low seismic velocity, is isotropic, and is resistive.

the resistivity and anisotropy of the sub- continental lithospheric mantle are determined by the bulk matrix property of temperature, with the iron content and composition of the matrix playing a lesser role, and the presence of interconnected conducting minor phases playing an insignificant role.
the resistivity of the lithospheric and asthenospheric mantle of southern Africa is primarily controlled by temperature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
electrical resistivity is a good predictor of seismic velocity, and vice versa.
the resistive regions are the most stable regions, and the most conductive regions are the least stable, and that diamonds occur preferentially on the boundaries of the two.

diamondiferous regions are located at the boundaries of the cratons and mobile belts, where the lithospheric thickness is reduced, and where the mantle is thermally and/or compositionally heterogeneous.
The main takeaway from our work is that
electrical resistivity and seismic velocity can be used to identify diamondiferous regions in the mantle and to predict their locations.
diamondiferous kimbertlites are preferentially found in regions where the lithospheric electrical resistivity is high and anisotropic, and where the seismic P- and S-wave velocities are also high.
the diamondiferous cratonic mantle is electrically resistive, and that diamondiferous kimblelites occur on the edges of cratons.
